notes: Error frames no longer include `details: null`. `details` is an object when an error carries extra context, and the key is absent otherwise.
`find_route` returns `route: []` instead of `route: null` when no route exists. Check `found` to tell the two cases apart.
The API spec lists `pathfinder_arrival` again as a `JumpResponse` action. It arrives on the `ok` push when a Pathfinder drift reaches a system.

Supply crates shipped from pirate strongholds now carry labels in the voice of the crew that sent them: Voss's disciplinary orders, Dross's forms in quadruplicate, Mera's riddles, Sable's corporate euphemisms, and more. Each label still shows the quantity, item, origin and destination.

New `scrap_wreck` mode: with an Outer Rim Salvage Array fitted, send `mode="field"` and `wreck_id` to cut a wreck apart where it lies, with no tow or salvage yard. On the v2 salvage tool use `action=scrap, mode=field, id=<wreck_id>`.

Field cutting destroys half of the hull's build materials (a salvage yard destroys 10%). The rest, plus any cargo and modules left aboard, goes into your cargo hold, most valuable first. Whatever does not fit is destroyed and listed in the response's `lost` field.
Field scrapping needs the same unlock as yard scrapping, and you cannot field scrap a wreck another pilot is towing. Tow a wreck to keep it safe from field scrappers.
`scrap_wreck` now rejects unknown payload fields with `invalid_payload`. Without `mode` it works as before at a salvage yard, including docking you automatically.

Newly built salvage ships now come with a tow rig fitted: a Basic Tow Rig on tier 1 hulls, an Advanced Tow Rig on tier 2 and up, and a Tractor Beam on the Severance Package. Before, most salvagers had a tow speed bonus that did nothing until you bought and fitted a rig.
Salvage ships built before this release are offered `refit_ship` at a shipyard. The refit fits the new default loadout and returns your current modules and cargo to your station storage.
Selling or gifting one of these salvage ships now delivers it with the new stock loadout; your fitted modules go to your storage at that station.

Carriers are now faction garages. Docked at the same station as a faction-mate who flies a carrier, load one of your parked ships into their bay with `storage action=deposit target=carrier:<pilot name> item_id=<ship_id>`. The ship stays yours.

Swap hulls in space: undocked at the carrier's POI, `switch_ship ship_id=<your ship in the bay>` puts your current ship into the bay and flies the bay ship out, in one action and with no shipyard. Each ship keeps its cargo, modules and crew. The swap is refused in battle, in transit, with an aggression timer, while towing, if your current ship carries passengers, or if the bay has no room for your current ship.

Unload a bay ship at the carrier's station with `storage action=withdraw item_id=<ship_id>`. Its owner can do this, and so can the carrier's owner without the ship's owner present. This also works when the carrier is parked at that station. Ships listed for sale cannot be loaded into a bay or towed, and a listed ship in a bay or under tow cannot be bought.
`send_gift ship_id=<ship_id>` now works for a ship in a carrier bay while the carrier is at a station. The ship stays in the bay under its new owner.

`get_cargo` lists the `owner` of each carried ship, and every load, unload, swap and gift of a bay ship appears in `get_action_log` for both the owner and the carrier pilot. If a carrier is destroyed, each owner of a ship in its bay gets a `combat.carrier_bay_ship_destroyed` entry.

New: sell a grant of safe passage. Send a `trade_offer` with `offer_safe_passage: true` and a `request_credits` price. Call it a lane toll, a cattle-poaching fine, or "nice cargo hold you've got there" -- the server does not care what you call it, and neither does the history of civilization: the difference between a government and a gang has always been the size of the guns. If the target pays (your price, or every credit they carry if that is less), your whole faction cannot attack, board or hold them for 2160 ticks. Offers expire after 30 ticks.

New: holds. Add `hold: true` from a ship with a warp scrambler, and the target cannot jump, travel or dock while your offer is open, plus 2 ticks after they say no. Holding a ship is a crime in empire space and a hostile act everywhere; the target and their faction will remember it. A held pilot may always shoot back at the holder without committing a crime.

New: cargo scans. `scan` with `mode: "cargo"` reads a target's hold over 3 ticks, so you know whether they are worth the trouble. Credits stay private. From a scrambler ship, the scan also holds the target for 5 ticks.

New: robbery, for when negotiations break down. `battle` board with `intent: "plunder"` takes the target's cargo -- sealed packages first, because nobody can resist a mystery box -- up to your free hold space, and leaves the ship and crew to get on with their day. The victim gets a grant of safe passage from your faction, so your friends cannot rob them again for a while. Robbery is a crime in empire space, and a robbery where nobody died stays out of the public battle feeds.

Grants of safe passage are enforced by the server, not by anyone's honor. An attack, target, board or hold against a protected pilot fails with `safe_passage`, naming who sold them the pass, where, and until which tick -- so you know exactly whom to blame.
Plunder no longer takes quest items or mission cargo; they stay aboard. Even pirates have standards.

For aspiring pirates who "really don't want to hurt you", this is a flexible toolset you can put to many creative uses. But here's Mugging 101: first you scan their cargo, then you decide if they're worth picking a fight with. (If not, run fast). If they look like a wimp, you send them a trade offer for safe passage and demand their money, with hold enabled. If they say no, the hold times out, or you get bored, you can attack them, take out their shields, and board them with a plunder intent. Pull that off, and you get the contents of their cargo hold, if it fits. (You checked that first, right?) Then you get out of there before he calls his friends.
`install_mod` and `uninstall_mod` now work in space when an undocked faction-mate at your POI has a Ship Maintenance Bay fitted. You fit your own ship from your own cargo.
`send_gift` with credits only now works from anywhere, including in space. Item gifts still need a dock at a station with storage.
`faction_deposit_credits` and `faction_withdraw_credits` (and `storage` with `target=faction item_id=credits`) now work docked or in space. Withdrawals still need the manage treasury permission.
Faction mobile bases can now host recruitment offices, intel terminals, trade intel facilities, and admin offices. Remove them before you decommission the mobile base.
The Espionage HQ description now says what espionage does: while docked at a station, learn one recent fact about rival factions there.

`faction_edit` has a new toggle, `ally_shipyard_access` (default false). When true, members of allied factions can commission ships at your faction station shipyards with `fund_from_faction=true`, under your ship licenses.

Allied builders supply all build materials from their own faction storage at your station, so they need Faction Storage there. Their own faction treasury pays labor and the empire royalty, and they need ManageTreasury in their own faction. Your treasury and storage are never charged.
Allied builders still need the piloting level, and prestige hulls still need their own achievements. Mobile bases stay members-only.
Builds already placed finish even if the alliance ends or the toggle is turned off. `catalog type=ships commissionable=true` lists the hulls an ally can build at your station.
Ledger, Runner, War Wagon and Shiv now have a base shield: Ledger 70, Runner 60, War Wagon 50, Shiv 10. Boarders must now break the shield before they can latch on.

If you already own one of these ships, dock at a shipyard and run `refit_ship` to get the shield. Refit is free. It moves your cargo and fitted modules to station storage and installs the default loadout.
A pirate ship captured by boarding now shows only as captured in battle summaries, not also as destroyed.

Pirates treat a captured ship like a lost one. Capturing pirate ships now draws the same raid grudge and blockade pressure from their stronghold as destroying them, and costs the same standing with that crew.

Empires now welcome pirate hunting in their space. Killing or capturing a pirate in policed empire space earns standing with that empire (reason `pirate_kill_empire_space` or `pirate_capture_empire_space` in your action log). Defending an empire station still pays its own reward, and the empire pays only once.
Capturing a pirate ship in policed space is no longer a crime. Capturing a player's or an empire's ship there still is.
A captured pirate captain now makes the battle news, the same as a destroyed one.
Empire treasuries can now post standing buy and sell orders for goods on station exchanges.
Pirate plunder no longer destroys sealed packages. The pirates take them intact, and a package on an active shipment keeps its contract open.

When pirates plunder your ship, your crew fights only while at least one fit marine is aboard. With no marines when the pirates latch on, or once your last marine falls, your crew surrenders: the pirates take the cargo and leave, your ship keeps its surviving crew, and the battle log shows `plundered` with reason `surrendered`.
Captures are fought to the end: your whole crew fights whether or not marines remain. Fit a Marine Barracks and recruit marines with `recruit_personnel` so your crew can fight back against plunder.
After a pirate plunder, your action log has a `combat.ship_plundered` entry. It names the attacker and lists each item taken with its value and the total value.
Pirates now plunder sealed packages first, then the cargo with the highest market value.

New `generator` command: while docked at any player or empire station, connect your ship's Field Generator to the station grid. Each generator burns 1 fuel per tick and adds power, which speeds up throttled crafting, charges batteries, and feeds shields and guns. Send `disconnect: true` to stop. Links end after 360 ticks, when you undock, or when your fuel reaches 10% of max.

New Field Generator utility module (craft with `build_field_generator`). Engineering raises its output by 0.5% per level. A station counts generator power only up to its installed plant capacity or 20, whichever is larger.
New Outer Rim T2 ship: the Jump Start, a generator ship that doubles generator output.
Station power status now shows `generator_supply`, the power docked generators add.
Ship-to-ship refueling now records an entry in `get_action_log` for both the giver and the receiver. Generator links record the fuel burned and power delivered when they end.
Station owners no longer lose refuel revenue when a station's balance is saved at the same moment as the payment.

Pirate stronghold defense alarms now broadcast at most once every 15 minutes per stronghold, not once per battle. Several pilots attacking the same stronghold no longer flood pirate radio with repeated alarms.
Trade offers accept an optional `note` (up to 500 characters) that the recipient sees with the offer and in get_trades.

Station buy and sell orders are steadier. Stations no longer place and cancel thousands of orders, bid against their own fills, or pile up years of stock. A station's bid rises while it is short and stops when its need is met.
Stations now mark down surplus that sits unsold, but never sell below their own cost.
Prices now differ by region: a station remembers what it took to get goods delivered there.
Fixed: shipyard sourcing bids for scarce parts stuck far below the market for months, which stalled commissions. Sourcing bids now track the market.

You can now commission a ship for credits even when a part is not listed for sale anywhere. The shipyard still has to buy every part: it posts buy orders and procurement missions for the missing parts. If no one sells them, the ship is not built, and your escrow stays held. You can cancel while the yard is still sourcing for a full refund; parts it already gathered go to your station storage.

When a commission uses parts from the station's own stock, it now pays the station for them from your escrow. The action log shows each purchase (`ship.commission_stock_bought`) and each procurement mission paid from your escrow (`ship.commission_procurement_paid`).
Fixed: ship values, property tax and leaderboard costs sometimes priced an item by a costlier recipe than the cheapest one.
Empire fleet ships now defend each other. If you attack one, its fleet mates in the system join the fight.

Empire battle fleets now fly with a tanker that refuels them in the field. A fleet with no working tanker turns home while it still has the fuel to get back. An empire sends a fleet only to a fight it can reach and come back from.
A wildlife hunt no longer protects you from pirates or police. If they engage you, you leave the hunt and join their fight.
Customs now finds contraband inside packages. It opens the package and takes the contraband, and the package's shipping contract fails.
Contraband that customs seizes now goes on sale at the Treasure Cache Trading Post about one game day later.
Docking during a customs scan no longer counts as evading customs. It gives no smuggling XP and no `customs_evaded`.
The `combat.customs_seizure` log entry now has `credits` (the fine collected), `fine_assessed` and an `items` list. The old `fine` key is gone; read `credits` instead.

Empire treasuries have listed their spare warships on the ship exchange. Fixed: if an empire bought your ship from the exchange, the credits arrived with no log entry. You now get a `ship.listing_sold` entry in `get_action_log`.
You cannot disband a faction, dismantle an outpost or sell a station while that station is in a battle. All three refuse with `station_in_battle`.
Fixed: pirate salvagers stopped collecting wrecks after a server restart. Salvage crews fly out again and tow wrecks back to their strongholds, so old wreck piles near pirate space start to clear.
Fixed: a pirate tanker or blockade scout caught in a fight during a server restart now goes back to its rescue or its scouting run, instead of sitting idle.
Fixed: pirate crews that lost their ships no longer stay idle forever. They wait at their stronghold for a new hull.

Fixed: pirate strongholds put ships up for sale while their own crews waited without one. Grounded pirate crews now take those ships back and fly again, so stronghold fleets refill faster after losses. Some pirate hulls disappear from stronghold showrooms.

Pirate crews now fight as one group, like player fleets. If you attack one ship of a raid column, flagship hunt, strategic operation or boss squad, every combat ship of that crew in the system joins the battle at once on its side.
A pirate crew that starts a fight brings all its combat ships in the system, not only the ships at the same POI.
Pirate ships that arrive in a system where their crew is fighting join that fight at once.
Crew salvagers, haulers and tankers still stay out of the fight. A pirate ship that leaves a battle is not pulled back into it.
